title: Vidya Balan
wiki_lead:
Vidya Balan (pronounced [ʋɪd̪ːja baːlən]; born 1 January 1979) is an Indian actress. Known for pioneering a change in the portrayal of women in Hindi cinema with her roles in female-led films, she is the recipient of several awards, including a National Film Award and seven Filmfare Awards. She was awarded the Padma Shri by the Government of India in 2014. 
Vidya aspired to a career in film from a young age and had her first acting role in the 1995 sitcom Hum Paanch. While pursuing a master's degree in sociology from the University of Mumbai, she made several unsuccessful attempts to start a career in film, and featured in television commercials and music videos. She made her film debut by starring in the Bengali film Bhalo Theko (2003) and received praise for her first Hindi film, the drama Parineeta (2005). This was followed by several commercial successes including Lage Raho Munna Bhai (2006) and Bhool Bhulaiyaa (2007), but her subsequent roles were met with negative reviews.
Vidya established herself by starring as headstrong women in five consecutive commercial successes, which also earned her critical and awards recognition. These were in the drama Paa (2009), the black comedy Ishqiya (2010), the thrillers No One Killed Jessica (2011) and Kahaani (2012), and the biopic The Dirty Picture (2011). The last of these won her the National Film Award for Best Actress. Following a downturn, Vidya made a career comeback by playing cheerful women balancing work and family life  in Tumhari Sulu (2017) and Mission Mangal (2019). She then starred in the Amazon Prime Video films Shakuntala Devi (2020), Sherni (2021), and Jalsa (2022), and in the theatrical releases Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3 (2024) and Jailer 2 (2026).
Vidya also promotes humanitarian causes and supports the empowerment of women. She is a member of the Indian Central Board of Film Certification and has hosted a radio show. Early in her career, she drew criticism for her fluctuating weight and dress sense, but was later credited in the media for her unconventionality. Vidya is married to the film producer Siddharth Roy Kapur.

Early life and initial career struggles
Vidya was born on 1 January 1979 in Bombay (present-day Mumbai) into a Tamil Brahmin Iyer family. Her father, P. R. Balan, worked as the executive vice-president of Digicable, and her mother, Saraswathy, is a homemaker. According to Vidya, they speak a mix of Tamil and Malayalam at her home in Palakkad, Kerala. Her elder sister, Priya Balan, works in advertising. Actress Priyamani is her second cousin. Vidya grew up in the suburban neighbourhood of Chembur and studied at St. Anthony Girls' High School.

grok_lead: Vidya Balan (born 1 January 1978) is an Indian actress primarily known for her versatile performances in Hindi cinema, where she has established herself as one of the leading contemporary actresses through roles that challenge stereotypes and celebrate female-centric narratives. She has received widespread acclaim for her acting prowess, earning prestigious honors such as the National Film Award for Best Actress, multiple Filmfare Awards, and the Padma Shri in 2014 for her contributions to the arts. Born in Ottapalam, Palakkad district, Kerala, to a Tamil-speaking Iyer family, Balan was raised in Chembur, Mumbai, by her father P. R. Balan, a former executive vice-president at Digicable, and her mother Saraswathy, a homemaker; she has an elder sister, Priya. She completed her schooling at St. Anthony Girls' High School in Chembur and pursued higher education in sociology, earning a bachelor's degree from St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, followed by a master's degree from the University of Mumbai. Her early interest in performing arts led her to participate in local theater and elocution competitions during school. Balan began her career in the entertainment industry as a teenager, appearing in over 90 television advertisements and featuring in music videos for artists such as Shubha Mudgal, Euphoria, and Pankaj Udhas. She made her acting debut on television with a supporting role in the popular sitcom Hum Paanch (1995â1999) and hosted shows on channels like Zee TV and Sahara TV in the early 2000s. Her film journey started with the unreleased Bengali movie Bhalo Theko (2003), opposite Jisshu Sengupta, before her Bollywood breakthrough in Sanjay Leela Bhansali's romantic drama Parineeta (2005), for which she won the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut. Following Parineeta, Balan appeared in commercially successful films like Lage Raho Munna Bhai (2006), Guru (2007), and Bhool Bhulaiyaa (2007), showcasing her range in comedic and dramatic roles, though she faced body-shaming and typecasting early on. Her career transformed with the critically acclaimed Paa (2009), earning her the Filmfare Award for Best Actress as the mother of a child with progeria, and further solidified with bold performances in Ishqiya (2010) and the biopic The Dirty Picture (2011), inspired by the life of actress Silk Smitha, which won her the National Film Award for Best Actress and another Filmfare. Subsequent hits including the thriller Kahaani (2012), for which she received a third Filmfare Best Actress award, and Tumhari Sulu (2017), her fourth such honor, highlighted her ability to lead women-centered stories to box-office success. In recent years, Balan has continued to diversify her portfolio with roles in Sherni (2021), a streaming drama about a forest officer; Jalsa (2022), a social thriller that earned her a Critics' Best Actress award at the Dadasaheb Phalke International Film Festival in 2023; the murder mystery Neeyat (2023); and romantic comedies Do Aur Do Pyaar (2024) and Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3 (2024), the latter marking her return to the horror-comedy franchise. On a personal note, she married producer Siddharth Roy Kapur, former CEO of UTV Motion Pictures, on 14 December 2012 in a traditional ceremony in Mumbai, and the couple has no children as of 2025; Balan is also known for her advocacy on women's empowerment, education, and health issues like HIV/AIDS.
